text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended a fairly busy day with prices holding steady at slightly higher levels. Most of the activities stemmed from switching out of the near August position ahead of its expiry. August closed $1.80 higher at $321.0 per tonne, while October ended $0.30 higher at $314.50 per tonne. In Paris August 45 ICUMSA ended at $321.50 per tonne, up $2.50, while October 100 ICUMSA was down $1.10 at $287.90 per tonne.

World raw sugar futures in New York ended a thinly traded session slightly lower. October lost 5 points to close at 11.06 cents/lb, while March ended 1 point lower at 11.24 cents/lb. The floodings in Poland and the Czech Republic will not have any material effect on the 1997/98 supply and demand balance. Otherwise the market was devoid of fresh fundamental market moving news.

IRELAND ** - Sugar exports in January 1997 reached 2,891 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 19,472 tonnes, down from 41,656 tonnes exported in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 74,907 tonnes, up from 56,773 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in 1996/97 was the United Kingdom with 17,019 tonnes whites against 19,607 tonnes in October/January 1995/96.

COSTA RICA ** - Sugar production in 1996/97 (December/November) reached 326,250 tonnes, tel quel, up from 332,000 tonnes produced the previous year, industry sources said. Consumption in 1996/97 is put at 183,000 tonnes, up from 179,200 tonnes in 1995/96. Molasses production in 1996/97 is likely to reach 125,000 tonnes, down from 129,560 tonnes produced the previous year.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG ** - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 53,463 tonnes, raw value, compared to 56,877 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 459,183 tonnes against 494,206 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 711,840 tonnes, down from 1.139 million tonnes imported in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 311,609 tonnes whites against 385,556 tonnes and Germany with 102,816 tonnes against 31,007 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 reached 111,728 tonnes, up from 60,330 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/March 1996/97 up to 771,467 tonnes compared to 716,629 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 988,722 tonnes, down from 1.566 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Syria with 120,829 tonnes whites against 123,497 tonnes, Saudi Arabia with 50,360 tonnes against 53,796 tonnes, Israel with 44,148 tonnes, down from 80,745 tonnes and Algeria with 39,654 tonnes, up from 4,252 tonnes.

FRANCE ** - Sugar consumption in January 1997 amounted to 180,013 tonnes, raw value, up from 170,160 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative consumption in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 721,521 tonnes compared to 662,459 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total consumption in 1995/96 reached 2.220 million tonnes compared to 2.184 million tonnes in 1994/95.
